# Save and rerun a task

Save a result you accepted, then use its code with another monthly file. Auto-Mate checks the new file against the saved task before starting. A file that fits goes through local code checks, your **Run it** approval, and the usual result review without opening an AI session.

## What It Does

A **saved task** owns a copy of the accepted run's code and tests, declared outputs, input shape, remembered decisions and answers, and the Python runtime on which that run was checked. It has numbered revisions. Saving an accepted repair adds the next revision; earlier revisions are kept unchanged, and the newest is used for new runs. **Saved tasks** lists the current revision, last run, and run count. The detail page shows expected files, required columns and types, outputs, remembered choices, runtime, revisions, code on request, and runs.

On the source task's run page, the run that produced a saved revision has a **Saved as** marker in the run rail. The marker links to the saved task and names its revision when it is later than revision 1. A task started with **Run with another file** shows its saved-task name and revision before Run 1; a task started through **Repair with AI** shows that repair origin there. These origin labels describe the saved revision used to start the task. The rail shows the runs of the current task, with the reason for each later run; it does not merge runs from other tasks that used the same saved task. If the saved task has since been deleted, its origin remains as a label without a saved-task link.

Remembered notes from the agent's questions use the choice's readable label, such as **A single web page**, instead of its internal value. If you answered in your own words, the note keeps your typed answer. An answered follow-up is kept as a separate question and answer.

The saved input shape includes file formats, worksheet names, column names and types. The save dialog states what is kept in these words:

> A saved task keeps column and sheet names, your filenames as labels, your answers, and code that may mention a value the AI saw. It keeps no data rows and survives deleting the task it came from.

For a fitting file, Auto-Mate checks the saved code again using synthetic rows shaped like the new file. The code then waits for your approval before it reads the real file. You review the outputs and say whether they did what you wanted. This path opens no AI provider session and records no new disclosure transmission. **Nothing sent to the AI is a statement about this path, not about execution isolation:** the Python code runs with this application's access, as it does for a first run.

## How to Use It

1. Finish a run and accept its result. On its run page, choose **Save this task**, review **What will be kept** and any computer-clock warning, give it a name, then choose **Save task**.
2. Open **Saved tasks**, select the task, and choose **Run with another file**. Fill every file slot with an analyzed CSV or Excel file. Choose an optional **as-of** date, or leave it at today. The fit check appears after all slots are filled.
3. Read the fit check. If the file fits, choose **Start**. Review the code checks and intent, choose **Run it**, then review the outputs. Accepting the result completes the run. A warning deserves review even when starting is allowed.
4. If a required column or worksheet is missing, choose the corresponding column or worksheet in the new file, or say that it is absent. Answer any new or conflicting decision and add a note if useful. Read **Instructions for the AI** and the new file's disclosure review before consenting to **Repair with AI**. The repair is a new generated run and passes through verification, approval, and result review.
5. After accepting a repair, use **Save this task** on its run page to add the next revision. You may instead save that accepted run as a new saved task. The original revision remains available to inspect.

For example, if a saved task used `Amount` and the new file has `Total`, choose `Total` for the missing column. Your choices are shown as fixed sentences, exactly as they will be sent, before you consent. Files are named by position, never by filename:

```text
Adapt the saved task for the new file using these choices:
In the first file, use the column “Total” wherever the saved task used “Amount”.
In the first file, the column “Region” no longer exists; do the task without it.
In the first file, the sheet “Oct” is the one the saved task called “Sep”.
For the column “Date” (how its dates are read), use “DD/MM/YYYY”.
```

Your optional note follows the sentences word for word. The repair sends the reviewed instructions and the **new** file's approved description to the AI; it does **not** send the saved code.

On a saved-code run, **Run again exactly** starts a linked run with that run's code, input files, and as-of date. It runs the checks and approval gate again. **Repair with AI** is the route for changing what the code does; it requires fresh disclosure consent. On the latest completed run, open **Run it again** below the result for these actions. If that run failed, find the retry actions in its outcome summary. While a run waits for your result review, use **Did this do what you wanted?**; rejecting a saved-code result records your feedback and offers replay or repair without automatically starting an AI retry. An earlier run links to the run that came from it instead of offering another retry control.

If you retry an AI run of the same task, Auto-Mate carries earlier answered agent questions into the new AI request. It uses readable choice labels and your typed answers, places a retained follow-up directly after its parent with a **Follow-up** prefix, and keeps the latest answer when question wording repeats. This carried context is limited to 4,000 characters. A saved-code run has no AI request, so it does not use this context.

## Understanding the fit check

The report has three outcomes: **This file fits the saved task’s recorded shape**, **This file fits, with warnings to review**, or **This file needs choices or repair before it can run**. A blocking finding prevents a saved-code start. Warnings allow a start but may affect the result. Information records an observation or a remembered decision.

| Finding shown in the report | What to check |
| --- | --- |
| The number of files is different; This file is still being analyzed | Fill every slot and wait for profiling. |
| The file format changed; A worksheet is missing | Supply the expected format or choose a worksheet mapping for an AI repair. |
| A required column is missing; A column has an incompatible type | Supply a file with the expected column and usable type, or review a repair. |
| A saved decision conflicts with this file; This file needs a new decision | Answer the question before an AI repair. A recorded date-order choice can conflict with an unambiguous date format in the new file. |
| A column type changed; A column is empty; This table has no data rows | Review whether the code and result still make sense. |
| The first worksheet has a new name; The saved code did not declare columns for this file | Review which worksheet and columns the code actually reads. |
| The Python environment changed; The Python environment is not ready | The saved runtime differs, or a comparison is unavailable. The code is checked on the current runtime before approval. |
| The code may use the computer clock; The code reads the computer clock | A chosen date might not control direct clock reads in the saved code. |
| A saved decision was applied; A saved decision is no longer needed | Check how an earlier choice was used for this file. |
| There are extra columns; An optional column is missing | These are reported but do not block a saved-code start. |

The check compares **shape and recorded choices**, not the meaning of the data. A column still named `Amount` could contain a different measure. Inspect the file, the approval intent, and the outputs before accepting them.

## Inputs and Outputs

Each saved file slot is associated with an original input name expected by the code. The new upload is used under that name for synthetic checks and the approved real-file run; your original upload is not reused for a new monthly run. The fit check returns its status, findings, remembered-rule counts, runtime comparison, as-of value, and a digest binding the displayed check to the selected uploads and revision. A changed selection or revision requires a fresh check before **Start**.

Every new run records an as-of instant, calendar date, and time zone. A chosen date must be real and no later than today in the selected time zone. Auto-Mate passes `AUTOMATE_AS_OF`, `AUTOMATE_AS_OF_DATE`, and `AUTOMATE_TIMEZONE` to Python. The code contract asks generated code to use these values, but the save-time clock scan is only a best-effort warning about direct clock reads.

**Run again exactly** preserves code, input files, and date; it uses today's locked Python environment. Python or package changes can alter results, and the approval gate names a detected runtime change. “Exactly” does not promise bit-for-bit output.

## Configuration and Permissions

This single-user local preview has no saved-task setting, account role, or per-user permission. The browser uses the local API; its write routes check the request's origin. Read routes rely on browser same-origin behavior, which is not protection from other programs or accounts on the computer. An AI provider is needed for a repair, and repair requires fresh consent for the new file's disclosure.

## Deleting and limits

Deleting the source task leaves its saved task and copied revision code in place. Deleting a saved task removes its revisions, but tasks and runs already made from it remain in History with their saved-task labels. An existing saved-code run can still be replayed from its own retained code and inputs. Deleting a saved task prevents starting a new run from that saved task.

The revision immutability rules stop the application from editing a saved revision; they do not protect the database from another program with write access, including unisolated generated code in this preview. A saved task stores no original data rows or reusable input file. There is no scheduler, task gallery, saved-task rename, or way to make an older revision current again. Replay of a generated run that did not use saved code is not available.
